newsitem.title: UK: Alert for African stowaways arriving in UK ports.
newsitem.headline: Alert for African stowaways arriving in UK ports.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major, informed on Thursday of a sudden spate of dead stowaways being found in the holds of ships in British ports, said West African countries and shipping companies needed to act to tackle the problem.
Major was alerted to the issue after Stuart Atkinson, coroner for South Humberside on England's east coast, wrote to his local member of parliament, Michael Brown.

Atkinson expressed his alarm that 10 people had been found stowed away on small ships of around 1,000 tonnes from Sierra Leone, Nigeria and Ivory Coast putting into Humberside ports over the past six months.
Seven of these had died of dehydration as they hid in cargoes of copra, cocoa or oilseeds, he said.
"This was not a problem I had encountered before," Atkinson told Reuters. "I am worried that perhaps this has become a trend and that other British ports have had similar incidents."
Brown, who raised the issue with Major during parliament's question time, urged him to ask Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind to discuss the problem with senior diplomats of the countries involved.
Replying, Major said: "We do need to examine both with the host countries and with the shipping lines better arrangements to ensure that they (stowaways) are not hidden away on their ships."
Atkinson said it might be that because the stowaways had not returned, people in West Africa imagined that they had succeeded in getting to Britain safely and were now living there.
He suggested that as well as tightening security in their ports, authorities in West Africa might publicise the fact that many had perished on the way to Britain.
